items.title: How the Ukraine War Became a Fight for the Skies
items.summary: Russia and Ukraine are producing ever larger numbers of innovative aerial weapons, hoping for a breakthrough as ground combat is largely frozen.

items.title: China’s Nonsmokers Try to Clear the Air, One Confrontation at a Time
items.summary: Disputes between smokers and nonsmokers are becoming more visible as a younger generation increasingly refuses to suffer secondhand smoke in silence.

items.title: How Being Cool Is Making The Hague a Vacation Hot Spot
items.summary: Looking for respite from European heat waves, summer tourists are flocking to the diplomatic hub. But city leaders are wary of overcrowding.

items.title: Israeli Strikes May Undermine Trump’s Peace Plan for Gaza
items.summary: President Trump announced a proposal aimed at achieving the disarmament of Hamas and an Israeli withdrawal. Israel ramped up attacks on the Palestinian enclave.

items.title: Finland Tries to Protect Children Against Deepfakes, With Russia in Mind
items.summary: Finland, wary of misinformation from Moscow and beyond, has a leg up on other nations in spotting fake news. But A.I. is a whole new challenge.

items.title: Russia’s Deadly Missile Attack on Kyiv Exploits Ukraine’s Depleted Air Defenses
items.summary: At least 17 people were killed, officials said, as the country runs desperately low on interceptor missiles that could fend off Russian bombardments.

items.title: Lobga Rangzen, the Tibetan Activist Who Set Himself on Fire in Manhattan
items.summary: No one doubted the intensity of Lobga Rangzen’s commitment to a Tibet free of Chinese control. But they were not prepared for what he did next.

items.title: A New Lethal Front in Ukraine: Its Beloved Gas Stations
items.summary: Russian drone attacks have hit hundreds of gas stations in apparent retaliation for Ukraine’s attacks on oil refineries.

items.title: Andy Burnham’s First Weeks as UK Prime Minister: TikToks, Podcasts and Promises
items.summary: Andy Burnham’s whirlwind of TikToks, podcasts and promises appears to be resonating with some voters. But he faces big decisions about how to pay for it all.

items.title: Pakistan’s Kashmir Problem
items.summary: A wave of protests is posing the most significant challenge in years to Islamabad’s authority in the region.

items.title: Disney+ Cracks Open the Door to TikTok Creator Videos
items.summary: Disney said it would allow “thoughtfully curated” fan-created videos, using clips from its library, to appear on the streaming service.

items.title: Wildfire Smoke and Airport Chaos: My Summer Vacation From Hell
items.summary: Used to chronicling other people’s vacation disasters, a travel reporter faced the new normal on her own long-awaited family trip.

items.title: Chipotle Removes Jalapeños Linked to Salmonella Outbreak From Its Restaurants
items.summary: The Minnesota Department of Health said it had identified 110 salmonella cases in this outbreak, and the F.D.A. is also investigating.

items.title: Appeals Court Says E.P.A. Cannot Block Billions in Climate Grants
items.summary: The funds have been frozen since early in President Trump’s second term.

items.title: Judge Sets Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger Trial for March
items.summary: Paramount, which struck a $111 billion deal to acquire Warner Bros., had requested a November trial for an antitrust lawsuit brought by state attorneys general.

items.title: SpaceX, in First Earnings After IPO, Reports Soaring AI Spending
items.summary: Elon Musk’s rocket company said its capital expenditures jumped nearly seven times from a year ago. Revenue also rose.

items.title: Justice Dept. Charges Doctor in $95 Million Skin Substitute Fraud Scheme
items.summary: Dr. Stephen Dubin, a wound care doctor in Nevada, is accused of applying unneeded, expensive wound coverings to seniors. He used the profits to buy yachts, the department said.

items.title: S&P 500 Hits Record High as Stock Market Worries About Iran and AI Ease
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 1.8 percent, pushing past its previous peak at the start of June and capping a big turnaround from a recent sell off in technology stocks.

items.title: Man’s Claim That Brakes Failed on Jaguar Was Scam to Avoid Car Payments, Court Rules
items.summary: Nathan Owen called the police, saying he was trapped in a runaway car. A judge determined it was a lie and sentenced him to more than four years in prison.

items.title: Medicaid Urges States to Increase Autism Therapy Oversight
items.summary: The program’s spending on the therapy has quintupled since 2021, far outstripping the growth in diagnoses and raising concerns about overprescribing and fraud.

items.title: In Lawsuit, NJ Accuses Amazon of Suppressing Pay for Delivery Drivers
items.summary: The state attorney general said in an antitrust lawsuit filed on Tuesday that the company was abusing its market power to keep its delivery costs low.

items.title: White House Whipsaws Silicon Valley (and Itself) Over A.I. Rules
items.summary: The Trump administration has struggled with how to approach “open source” models, which are freely available to download and favored by Chinese companies.

items.title: What Are Companies Getting for All That A.I. Spending?
items.summary: A new field of “tokenomics” has emerged to measure the return on all the money companies are pouring into artificial intelligence.

items.title: Trump White House Readies AI Framework to Review Security Risks
items.summary: The voluntary review process will cover closed-source artificial intelligence models, but exclude those that publish the underlying code.

items.title: A SpaceX Rocket Will Soon Crash Into the Moon
items.summary: The second stage of a Falcon 9 rocket, which sent two private landers to the moon last year, will collide with the moon early Wednesday morning.

items.title: SpaceX’s Stock Lockup Is Expiring. Prepare for a Bumpy Ride.
items.summary: On Thursday, employees and other insiders at Elon Musk’s rocket company will be released from their first stock “lockup” and can start selling some of their shares.

items.title: If You Can’t Beat A.I., Outdress It, Tech Firms and Their Swag Say

items.title: Google Earth Disables A.I. Tool After One Day Over Disinformation Concerns
